p.RUNNING-THE-STANDING-SWEEP: You are running the standing sweep from the Discipline's Sweep Playbook (`spec://org.vibevm.ai-native/core-ai-native/04-SWEEP-PLAYBOOK` — the shipped copy is at `vibedeps/flow-core-ai-native/<version>/spec/04-SWEEP-PLAYBOOK.md`; read it once per session if you have not).

item.TRUTH-GATES-ARE-THE-FLOOR: **the gates are the floor, the sweep is the ceiling**,

item.TRUTH-GATE-IS-TRUTH: and **the gate is truth, the collector is a guide**.

p.NEVER-SWEEP-ON-A-RED-TREE: Never sweep on a red tree.

p.ACT-ON-COLLECTOR-FACTS: Act on collector facts, never on memory.

p.ALL-COMMANDS-ARE-THE-SHIPPED-TOOLCHAIN: All commands below are the shipped toolchain.

p.IF-NOT-ON-PATH-INSTALL-OR-RUN-IN-PLACE: If `typescript-ai-native` is not on PATH, either install it once — `cargo install --path vibedeps/<stack-slot>/crates/typescript-ai-native-cli` — or run it in place: `cargo run --manifest-path vibedeps/<stack-slot>/Cargo.toml -p typescript-ai-native-cli --bin typescript-ai-native -- <args>`.

p.FLOOR-HAS-SEVEN-STEPS: Seven steps: prettier → tsc → tests → eslint → conform → specmap → test-gate.

p.RED-FLOOR-ADMITS-ONLY-GREENING-WORK: Red? The only legal work is making it green — fix, do not proceed.

p.CHECK-THE-PRINTED-POLICY-LINES: Check the printed policy lines: a `NO conform.toml — topology default in force` line means the project is not bootstrapped (`typescript-ai-native init`) and any green under it is vacuous, and every `DISABLED by policy` line is a standing decision to re-question weekly — a floor that shrank quietly is the failure mode this line exists to catch.

p.READ-THE-HEALTH-SUMMARY: Read the summary (the JSON at `discipline/health/latest-typescript.json` is the work-list; its git diff is the trend).

p.take-cheapest-wins-lead: Take one or two cheapest wins:

item.RATCHET-DANGER-BAND-FILES: **danger-band files** — split any file at the top of the [540,600) band before an edit trips the 600 budget; the new module keeps (or gains) its own `@scope` marker so the orphan gate never regresses.

item.RATCHET-UNREASONED-SUPPRESSIONS: **unreasoned suppressions** — every `@ts-expect-error` WITHOUT `-- reason` in the census is unrecorded testimony: add the reason or fix the underlying type. `@ts-ignore` is never acceptable — replace with `@ts-expect-error -- reason` and watch it fail when the error goes.

item.RATCHET-EXPORT-DOC-EXAMPLE-COVERAGE: **export doc-example coverage** — exports without an `@example` (or fenced block) are retrieval gaps; document the highest-traffic seam first.

item.RATCHET-ORPHAN-BACKLOG: **orphan backlog** — untagged exports the ratchet will block on: tag the export (`@implements spec://…`), `@scope` its file, or move it out of the public surface.

item.WEEKLY-FAST-LOOP: `typescript-ai-native fast-loop` — every cell answers inside the budget; a cell with NO tests fails the check (the loop must exist).

item.WEEKLY-TRIPWIRE: `typescript-ai-native tripwire --base origin/main` — debt that this week's changes touched; each fired entry is addressed in the PR text: pulled-in, re-dispositioned, or consciously deferred.

item.WEEKLY-REREAD-DISABLE-AND-EXEMPT-LISTS: Re-read the `floor_disable` list and the `[[typescript.exempt]]` list: does each reason still hold?

p.END-EVERY-SWEEP-WITH-THE-OUTCOME-TABLE: End every sweep with an outcome table — this stack's own addition, and not something the Sweep Playbook prescribes: per tier, what ran, what was found, the ONE ratchet item taken, and what was deliberately left (with why). The Playbook's own closing contract is its §4 «Output of a sweep» — topic-grouped commits, the refreshed health snapshot, the resume pointer — and it holds here unchanged.

p.green-gates-only-is-not-a-sweep: A sweep that only reports green gates did the floor's job, not the sweep's.

generation-time-assistant.title: The generation-time assistant (before you edit, not instead of the floor)

p.STACK-SHIPS-AN-AGENTIC-TYPE-ORACLE: The stack ships an agentic type oracle.

p.check-the-hypothetical-content-lead: Before writing a nontrivial `.ts` edit, check the HYPOTHETICAL content instead of paying a red floor iteration:

generation-time-assistant.fence: vibe bin exec typescript-ai-native-tcg -- validate src/cells/<cell>/index.ts \ --content-from - --root . # the edit on stdin; exit 1 = would fail

p.MCP-ALTERNATIVE: or, when the vibevm MCP server is mounted, call `tcg_validate` with the `content` argument (plus `tcg_scope` / `tcg_complete` / `tcg_type` for in-scope symbols, type-valid completions, and quick info).

p.RESPONSES-CARRY-THE-SAME-CONFORM-FINDING: Responses carry the SAME conform findings as the gate, flagged `baselined` or new, with guide-citing advice — a new finding in the answer means the floor WILL go red if you write that edit.

p.FLOOR-STAYS-THE-TRUTH: The floor stays the truth; the oracle exists so you reach it green on the first try.
